The answer says Shift+Enter and Enter both send `\r` in a classic terminal. It explains that the difference only arrives via the kitty/CSI u protocol or modifyOtherKeys, which the app must request and the outer terminal must support (with a per-terminal table).

It says tmux drops the modifier and gives `set -s extended-keys on` plus the terminal-features extkeys line. That clearly implies the option is not on by default, though the answer never says 'off by default' outright.
It recommends Alt+Enter and Ctrl+J as fallbacks, but never says to tell users which key inserts a newline. The only docs advice is about the tmux config lines.
It tells the developer to accept Ctrl+J and Alt+Enter 'anyway' because they work everywhere without setup. Shift+Enter is added on top as an enhancement.

Explains that terminals send the same `\r` for Enter and Shift+Enter by default, and that Shift+Enter only gets its own sequence when kitty keyboard protocol or modifyOtherKeys is enabled 'when the terminal supports them' (it notes Terminal.app does not).
Gives `set -s extended-keys on` for tmux 3.2+ and says tmux won't pass Shift+Enter through without it, which conveys that the option is off by default.
Recommends always accepting Ctrl+J and Alt+Enter, and showing a hint such as 'Enter send · Ctrl+J / Alt+Enter newline' in the input area.
Puts the keys that work in every terminal first ('regardless of anything else') and treats Shift+Enter via extended modes as an enhancement used only when supported.

Says Enter and Shift+Enter both send \r in the legacy encoding and become distinct only via the kitty keyboard protocol or xterm modifyOtherKeys, which the outer terminal must support (lists which terminals do and don't).
Says tmux 'needs extra config' and gives `set -s extended-keys on` plus extkeys terminal-features, which implies the option is off by default.
Recommends Ctrl+J and Alt+Enter as fallbacks and says to show a hint such as 'Ctrl+J / Alt+Enter for newline' in the input area.
Says to support the fallback keys even when extended reporting is enabled, keeping Ctrl+J and Alt+Enter, which work in the legacy encoding, alongside Shift+Enter.
